en.question: Question:
en.basics_denominator_01: Here at Fraction Farms, we showcase how to divide up land in order to produce crops more efficiently.
en.basics_denominator_02: We do this by taking Unit Tiles and breaking their sides into fractional lengths.
en.basics_denominator_03: There is a back and forward button to change the number of parts each side is divided up by, the first fraction goes horizontal, the second vertical.
en.basics_denominator_04: Let's use them to divide up this piece of farm land. Click the hint button if you need help. Click the submit button to check your results.
en.basics_denominator_05: Excellent! Let's try a different combination.
en.basics_numerator_01: Good job! From here, we need to identify the portion of land we want to use now that it is divided.
en.basics_numerator_02: We use the side buttons to highlight a portion of tiles.
en.basics_numerator_03: We then need to click on the individual pieces that intersect with the highlighted portions.
en.basics_numerator_04: Click submit once you think you have selected the right number of tiles.
en.basics_multiply_01: You're a fast learner! Great job!
en.basics_multiply_02: Notice how the solution we are getting is the same as if we multiplied the fractions by multiplying the numerators together and the denominators together.
en.basics_multiply_05: Wonderful! You've mastered working with one tile, but dividing up land sometimes takes multiple tiles.
en.basics_multiply_06: Let's move onto another part of the farm!
en.basics_error_denominator: Use the back and forward buttons on each side to divide the land based on the denominators.
en.basics_error_denominator_x: You have the vertical part of the tile divided. Now use the back and forward buttons on the horizontal size to divide the land based on the first denominator.
en.basics_error_denominator_y: You have the horizontal part of the tile divided. Now use the back and forward buttons on the vertical size to divide the land based on the second denominator.
en.basics_error_highlight: You have the tile divided correctly, but you need to highlight the land according to the numerators.
en.basics_error_highlight_x: You have the vertical part of the tile highlighted and divided. Now highlight the horizontal part of the land according to the first numerator.
en.basics_error_highlight_y: You have the horizontal part of the tile highlighted and divided. Now highlight the vertical part of the land according to the second numerator.
en.basics_error_numerator: You have the tile divided and highlighted correctly. Now just click on the tiles associated with the green intersection.
en.basics_error_reverse: You divided the land up correctly, but remember that the first fraction should be applied horizontally, and the second fraction vertically.
en.mixed_denominator_01: We need more than one tile when were dealing with numbers greater than one. For these problems, we have a four unit by two unit area to work with.
en.mixed_denominator_02: The whole number of the fractions relates to which tile the intersection occurs. Click on that tile to make the dividing and highlighting controls appear.
en.mixed_denominator_03: These tiles are interconnected. When you divide up one, it applies that to the other tiles in the row or column.
en.mixed_denominator_04: If you think you selected the wrong tile, it's okay. When you divide up the correct one, the previous division will be made whole again.
en.mixed_denominator_05: Let's focus on dividing up the land first. We'll come back to highlighting and portioning it after we master dividing.
en.mixed_multiply_01: Good job! Now let's move onto portioning the land with multiple tiles.
en.mixed_multiply_02: Highlighting still works the same as before, but now the highlighting extends to the tiles behind the selected one.
en.mixed_multiply_03: We still click on the pieces to select them, but because we are dealing with mixed tiles of fractional size, we convert the value to the common denominator.
en.mixed_multiply_05: Great job! Notice how the same rule applies, that we get the same solution had we multiplied the two numbers together.
en.mixed_multiply_08: I'm impressed! You've done really well to come this far!
en.mixed_multiply_09: You know, there is another way we can look at these problems that reference back to when we used one tile. Come on, I'll show you!
en.mixed_error_denominator: Remember to divide up the tiles using the forward and back buttons to match each denominator.
en.mixed_error_denominator_x: You have the vertical part of the tile divided. Now use the back and forward buttons on the horizontal size to divide the land based on the first denominator.
en.mixed_error_denominator_y: You have the horizontal part of the tile divided. Now use the back and forward buttons on the vertical size to divide the land based on the second denominator.
en.mixed_error_tile: The tile you divided was divided correctly, but it was not the correct tile. Use the whole numbers to determine which tile you need to divide up.
en.mixed_error_highlight: You have the land divided correctly, but is not highlighted properly. Use the highlighter to find the intersection of the two fractional lengths.
en.mixed_error_highlight_x: You have the vertical part of the tile highlighted and divided. Now highlight the horizontal part of the land according to the first numerator.
en.mixed_error_highlight_y: You have the horizontal part of the tile highlighted and divided. Now highlight the vertical part of the land according to the second numerator.
en.mixed_error_numerator: You have the tile divided and highlighted correctly. Now just click on the tiles associated with the green intersection.
en.mixed_error_reverse: You divided the land up correctly, but remember that the first fraction should be applied horizontally, and the second fraction vertically.
en.improper_line_01: Another way we can visualize using multiple tiles is by slicing up all the tiles by the same denominators, and counting the individual tiles up together.
en.improper_line_02: This will require us to look at our fractions as improper fractions. Let's take the problem we just completed and do it again, but looking at it as improper fractions.
en.improper_line_03: Well done! Now, on your own, convert the problem to improper fractions and solve the next problems using this method.
en.improper_line_04: Nicely done! Let's try the next one!
en.improper_line_05: Excellent! Just one more to go.
en.improper_line_06: Bravo! You've become quite the expert at being able to divide up land.
en.hint_submit: Everything looks good. Just click on the submit button to submit your answer.
